[[Houston, Texas]] | coordinates = {{coord|29.75768|-95.36906|region:US-TX|display=inline,title}} | status = completed | completion_date = 1980 | building_type = Commercial offices | roof = {{convert|230|m|abbr=on}} | floor_count = 55 | elevator_count = 27 | cost = | floor_area = {{convert|135500|m2|abbr=on}} | architect = [[Skidmore, Owings & Merrill]] | structural_engineer = | main_contractor = | developer = Hines Interests Limited Partnership | owner = Fantome Tower | operator = [[Hines Interests Limited Partnership]] | references = {{CTBUH|1093}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.emporis.com/buildings/117765 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306203218/https://www.emporis.com/buildings/117765 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=March 6, 2016 |title=Emporis building ID 117765 |work=[[Emporis]]}}{{Glass Steel and Stone|2016}}{{SkyscraperPage|251}}{{Structurae|20012171}} }} '''Enterprise Plaza''' (also known as '''1100 Louisiana''') is a 55-story, {{convert|230|m|abbr=on}} [[skyscraper]] at 1100 Louisiana Street in [[downtown Houston]], [[Texas]] The headquarters of [[Enterprise Products]] is located in the Enterprise Plaza. Enterprise Plaza was completed in 1980 by Hines. It was sold in 1985 to Capitol Guidance Corporation which sold it again to National Office Partners Limited Partnership (NOP), a joint venture between [[Hines Interests Limited Partnership]] and the [[California Public Employees Retirement System]] (CalPERS). Hines Real Estate bought the tower in January 2000. Enterprise Plaza is an office building located in the heart of Houston's energy and financial corridor. It stands at 756 ft (230 m) tall with 55 stories. Enterprise Plaza (also known as 1100 Louisiana) is a 55-story, 230 m (750 ft) skyscraper at 1100 Louisiana Street in downtown Houston, Texas The headquarters of Enterprise Products is located in the Enterprise Plaza.
Enterprise Plaza was completed in 1980 by Hines. It was sold in 1985 to Capitol Guidance Corporation which sold it again to National Office Partners Limited Partnership (NOP), a joint venture between Hines Interests Limited Partnership and the California Public Employees Retirement System (CalPERS). Hines Real Estate bought the tower in January 2000.
Enterprise Plaza is an office building located in the heart of Houston's energy and financial corridor. It stands at 756 ft (230 m) tall with 55 stories. It was the tallest building in Texas from 1980 until 1982 when it was surpassed by the JPMorgan Chase Tower.
